headline: Data centre builders are now ordering generators two years ahead, before their designs are final, because equipment and skilled workers are scarce.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 4: the panel was on 14 Oct 2026, two days before the window, and it rests on speakers' accounts at one conference rather than market data.
importance_line: Equipment and skilled labour shortages could delay AI data centre openings, which affects the companies and communities waiting on them, though the evidence is speakers' accounts at one conference rather than market-wide data.
summary: ET Datacenters reports, from a panel at the Capacity Europe 2026 conference on 14 Oct 2026, that data centre builders now commit to equipment makers before designs are final because generators can take two years to arrive and high-voltage transformers 12 to 18 months, according to Ozgur Duzgunoglu, head of engineering and design at Telehouse, a data centre operator. Speakers said speed now matters more than price, with Nelson Pinto de Magalhaes of the data centre developer Start Campus describing the approach as 'Procure first, design around it', and the article adds that Oracle has issued a force majeure notice (a legal notice excusing delays) for its Project Jupiter campus in New Mexico over possible power delays.
notes: Read in full. The shared fulltext copy was empty, so the page was fetched once directly. Panel was held 14 Oct 2026; ET Datacenters published 16 Oct 2026. Capacity Media's own page was blocked (403).
